docs.summary: A user assembly definition. Splits user scripts into a separately compiled assembly with its own references and platform constraints. Stored as a Prowl-native (Echo) text file with the `.asmdef` extension; the file is the source of truth and is edited through the inspector. Assembly definitions are pure compile-time metadata and never ship in a build.
Output assembly name (also how other asmdefs reference this one).
Names of other assembly definitions this assembly depends on.
If non-empty, the assembly is only included on exactly these platforms. Mutually exclusive with [`ExcludePlatforms`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Projects.Scripting.AssemblyDefinition~ExcludePlatforms).
If non-empty, the assembly is included everywhere except these platforms.

When true (default), the project's default assemblies automatically reference this one, so loose scripts can use its types without an explicit reference. When false, only assemblies that list it in [`References`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Projects.Scripting.AssemblyDefinition~References) can see it.

When true, only the plugins in [`PrecompiledReferences`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Projects.Scripting.AssemblyDefinition~PrecompiledReferences) are referenced (auto-referenced managed plugins are not added automatically).
Managed plugin file names (e.g. "MyLibrary.dll") referenced explicitly. Only consulted when [`OverrideReferences`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Projects.Scripting.AssemblyDefinition~OverrideReferences) is true.
Scripting define symbols that must all be set for this assembly to be compiled.
When true the assembly does not reference the engine assemblies (Prowl.Runtime/Editor).
Whether this assembly is compiled/included for the given platform name.
True when the assembly is usable in the editor but on no player platform: it should be available for editor tooling/reflection but must never be shipped in a build.
Serializes this assembly definition to an EchoObject compound for storage in the .asmdef file.
Deserializes an AssemblyDefinition from an EchoObject previously produced by ToEcho().
Writes this assembly definition to a file at the given path in Echo text format.
Reads an AssemblyDefinition from a .asmdef file. Returns a default definition with the file name as the assembly name if the file is empty.
